source_evidence: When you buy a share of common stock, you own equity in the company and will receive any dividends declared and paid by the company. When you buy a corporate bond, you do not own equity in the company.
question: How does owning a corporate bond differ from owning common stock?
answer: Common stock represents equity ownership in a company, and shareholders may receive dividends the company declares. A corporate bond is a debt obligation: bondholders do not own equity and instead have a legal claim to interest and, in most cases, repayment of principal. Unlike bond payments, dividends are not a payment the company is legally obligated to make to shareholders.
